title: Charlie Jacobs, the advanced trumpeter
summary: McGhee praises Harriet Calloway's trumpeter Charlie Jacobs as modern as Roy Eldridge with a beautiful tone, and tells how he fell apart when she left.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Now, that was the trumpet player, what was his name, Charlie Jacobs?
Charlie Jacobs, right. He was a helluva trumpet player, too, man. I used to marvel at this cat every night. Every time he played he was somethin' else.
You told me he was quite advanced...
For the time, he was somethin' else, man. I tell you, he was a bad motherfucker, that's all I can tell you -- because he was bad.
What kind of style did he play in, would you say, if
you could liken it to any style that we know? Was it a little like Roy Eldridge?

Well, he was just as modern as Roy was in them days. But he didn't play like Roy. He had a nice sound, though. He had a nice tone. And he could play. I used to marvel at him. I used to say, 'I wish I could play like that.'
And he was going with Harriet Calloway...
And when she cut out, he...

Yeah, he flipped. He didn't know what to do. But he followed her all the way to Seattle, you know; and they had quite a problem out there, I hear. But anyway, they didn't get back together. So I don't know what happened to him. I never heard of him any more. But he was a helluva trumpet player, though, man. I brag about him now. I was telling Dizzy about him. Charlie Jacobs was somethin' else. He had such a beautiful sound, man. You know, when he played, you couldn't help but listen.

So now, getting back to where I was at...
